whyWrongByChoice.B: Breaching her confidentiality is not required simply because she is a minor seeking sexual health care.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An exam looking for abuse is not indicated when her assessment raises no concern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Being younger than 18 and sexually active is not by itself reportable maltreatment; the full set of factors must be assessed.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with facial bruising discloses intimate partner violence. After discussing options, she declines referral to a shelter and chooses to return home with a safety plan she helped design. The physician respects her decision and arranges follow-up. Which ethical principle is most directly upheld?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autonomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Beneficence

choices.label: C
choices.text: Justice

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nondiscrimination

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nonmaleficence

explanation.summary: Respecting an informed survivor's own choices about her care and safety upholds autonomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autonomy is one of the four foundational principles of biomedical ethics applied to survivor care. Trauma-informed care seeks to preserve patient autonomy, and the patient's own goals and priorities should guide safety planning; honoring her informed decision to decline a shelter reflects autonomy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Beneficence (acting for her benefit) might favor the shelter; it is not the principle honored by deferring to her choice.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Justice concerns fair and equitable treatment and resource allocation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nondiscrimination is a guiding principle about equal care across groups, not about honoring her decision.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nonmaleficence concerns avoiding harm, not respecting her decision-making.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 12 weeks' gestation attends her first prenatal visit. On the intake form she notes that she underwent a genital procedure as a child in her country of origin. She appears calm and has no current complaints. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask which terms she prefers and what concerns she has

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume she is traumatized and refer her to counseling

choices.label: C
choices.text: Avoid the subject so as not to stigmatize her culture

choices.label: D
choices.text: Explain that her community's practice is inherently harmful

choices.label: E
choices.text: Schedule deinfibulation before discussing her goals

explanation.summary: Cultural humility with FGM means asking the patient's preferred terminology, concerns, and goals rather than assuming how she experiences it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clinicians should not assume that a patient endorses, rejects, regrets, or identifies as traumatized by FGM. The clinician should ask about the terminology the patient prefers, current symptoms or concerns, prior health experiences, sexual and reproductive goals, pregnancy or childbirth concerns, and her preferences regarding examination or treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Assuming trauma contradicts cultural humility; individual experiences of FGM differ.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Avoiding the topic neglects potential obstetric and gynecologic concerns she may have.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clinicians should avoid characterizing entire communities as harmful.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Procedures are planned around the patient's goals and preferences, not before learning them.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is evaluated in the emergency department after reporting a sexual assault. An officer accompanying her asks the physician to document whether her hymen is intact so that investigators can establish her prior sexual history. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An intact hymen excludes a penetrative assault

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hymen appearance separates consensual from forced sex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hymen findings do not reliably reveal sexual history

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hymen inspection is a standard forensic component

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hymenal tears reliably date the last intercourse

explanation.summary: Hymen appearance does not reliably indicate prior sexual activity in postpubertal individuals, and virginity examinations are not recommended.
explanation.whyCorrect: WHO does not recommend inspection of the genitalia to assess virginity. Physical findings, including the appearance or presence of a hymen, do not reliably indicate prior sexual activity in postpubertal individuals, and in sexual assault evaluation such examinations provide no useful evidence about sexual history.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hymen findings are unreliable indicators of sexual activity; an intact hymen does not exclude penetration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Physical findings of the hymen cannot establish whether sexual activity was consensual.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Such examinations are specifically not recommended as part of the sexual assault assessment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The hymen cannot reliably indicate prior sexual activity, much less date it.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 33-year-old uninsured woman arrives at the emergency department of a hospital covered by EMTALA with facial fractures after an assault. A registration clerk suggests redirecting her to a county clinic because she cannot pay. Under EMTALA, which of the following must the hospital provide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A screening exam, then stabilization or transfer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forensic evidence collection before any treatment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Police notification before examination can begin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transfer to a SANE facility before any screening

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treatment only once insurance or payment is verified

explanation.summary: EMTALA requires a medical screening examination and, if an emergency condition is found, stabilizing treatment or appropriate transfer.
explanation.whyCorrect: In emergency settings, EMTALA requires covered hospitals to provide an appropriate medical screening examination and, when an emergency medical condition is identified, stabilizing treatment within the hospital's capabilities or an appropriate transfer. Ability to pay does not change this obligation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Forensic collection is optional and patient-directed; it is not an EMTALA prerequisite to care.
whyWrongByChoice.C: EMTALA does not make screening contingent on police notification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Transfer before a screening exam bypasses the required medical screening examination.
whyWrongByChoice.E: EMTALA screening and stabilization are not conditioned on payment or insurance.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman tells her physician that her husband has confiscated her passport, forbids her from leaving the house alone, and says he will hurt her family if she disobeys. He has never struck her. Which statement best characterizes her situation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: GBV only if sexual assault has also taken place

choices.label: B
choices.text: GBV, because coercion and loss of liberty qualify

choices.label: C
choices.text: Not GBV, because acts within marriage are excluded

choices.label: D
choices.text: Not GBV, because no physical injury has occurred

choices.label: E
choices.text: Not GBV, because the harm is not sexual in nature

explanation.summary: GBV includes not only physical, mental, or sexual harm but also threats, coercion, and other deprivations of liberty.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gender-based violence encompasses acts that inflict physical, mental, or sexual harm or suffering, the threat of such acts, coercion, and other deprivations of liberty. Confiscating her passport, restricting movement, and threatening her family fit this definition even without physical injury.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sexual assault is not required; coercion and deprivation of liberty suffice.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intimate partner violence, including within marriage, is the most common form of GBV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Threats, coercion, and deprivation of liberty count as GBV without physical injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GBV includes mental harm and coercion, not only sexual harm.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman presents with pelvic pain. She reports that an older man she met online, who is not her boyfriend, gives her a place to stay in exchange for her having sex with men he arranges. He holds her identification and says she owes him money. Which form of gender-based violence is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Harmful traditional cultural practice

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intimate partner violence

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reproductive coercion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sex trafficking and exploitation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual orientation-based violence

explanation.summary: Sex trafficking and sexual exploitation involve commercial or other sexual activity obtained through force, fraud, coercion, or exploitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sex trafficking and sexual exploitation are defined as commercial or other sexual activity involving force, fraud, coercion, exploitation, or circumstances in which meaningful consent cannot be given. Sex arranged by a third party in exchange for housing, with her ID withheld and a debt imposed, fits this form.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Harmful cultural practices include FGM, forced marriage, and virginity testing, not commercial sexual exploitation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The man is explicitly not an intimate partner, so this is not IPV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coercive control of reproductive decisions is not what is described; the sex is arranged with others for his benefit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nothing indicates violence tied to her sexual orientation, gender identity, or expression.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 20-year-old college student reports that she agreed to have intercourse with a classmate, but partway through she told him to stop and he continued. She asks whether this counts as assault because she initially agreed. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consent given at the outset covers the whole encounter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nonconsensual acts require the use of a weapon or force

choices.label: C
choices.text: Once consent is withdrawn, proceeding is sexual violence

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only an initial refusal can make the act nonconsensual

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withdrawing consent requires physical resistance to count

explanation.summary: Consent is voluntary and freely given, and it can be withdrawn at any time.
explanation.whyCorrect: Consent is a voluntary, informed, and freely given agreement that can be withdrawn at any time. Sexual acts without consent are nonconsensual and constitute sexual violence, so continuing after she said stop is sexual violence regardless of her initial agreement.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Consent can be withdrawn at any time; initial agreement does not cover the whole encounter.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coercion by threats, or lack of consent alone, makes an act nonconsensual without a weapon.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Withdrawal of consent partway through makes further acts nonconsensual.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Consent is withdrawn by her statement; physical resistance is not required.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman reports that a man forced her to the ground and pushed an object slightly into her vulva before a passerby interrupted him and he fled. She asks what the act is legally called. Which of the following best classifies the act?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attempted rape, because he was interrupted

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attempted rape, because penetration was incomplete

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coercion, because no weapon was displayed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rape, because any degree of penetration qualifies

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unwanted contact, because no penis was involved

explanation.summary: Rape is physically forced or coerced penetration, even if slight, of the vulva or anus with a penis, other body part, or object.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rape occurs when there is physically forced or coerced penetration, even if slight, of the vulva or anus using a penis, other body parts, or an object. Slight forced penetration with an object meets the definition regardless of the interruption; attempted rape describes an attempt without penetration.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Interruption after penetration does not reduce the act to an attempt.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Penetration need only be slight; completeness is not required.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coercion is forcing involuntary action by threats or force; physical penetration here meets the rape definition.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The definition includes penetration with other body parts or an object, not only a penis.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A clinician working in a humanitarian clinic evaluates a girl brought in several hours after a female genital cutting procedure. Which of the following complications is most likely to be encountered in this immediate period?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic pelvic pain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemorrhage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infertility

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obstructed labor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual dysfunction

explanation.summary: Short-term complications of FGM include severe pain, hemorrhage, swelling, fever, infection, urinary problems, shock, and death.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the short term, FGM is associated with severe pain, hemorrhage, genital tissue swelling or injury, fever, infection, urinary problems, wound-healing problems, shock, and death. Hemorrhage is an immediate complication, whereas obstetric, gynecologic, and sexual problems develop later.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic pain is by definition a long-term, not immediate, consequence.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gynecologic problems are long-term rather than immediate complications.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obstetric problems are long-term complications that arise years later at childbirth.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Negative effects on sexual health are long-term complications.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman awakens in a friend's apartment with no memory of the night after becoming severely intoxicated and losing consciousness at a party. A man at the party later says they had intercourse and that she "never said no." Which statement is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consent is implied because she attended the party

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is not sexual violence without physical force

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is sexual violence only if threats were used

choices.label: D
choices.text: It was consensual because she did not verbally object

choices.label: E
choices.text: It was nonconsensual because she could not consent

explanation.summary: Sexual acts with a person unable to consent, from lack of capability or understanding, are nonconsensual and constitute sexual violence.
explanation.whyCorrect: Any sexual acts involving individuals who either do not give consent or are unable to give it (from lack of capability or understanding) are nonconsensual and are acts of sexual violence. An unconscious, severely intoxicated person lacks the capability to consent, so absence of objection is irrelevant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Consent is a voluntary, informed agreement to the activity itself, not implied by attendance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Inability to consent makes the act nonconsensual without physical force.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Threats are one route to coercion, but inability to consent alone makes the act sexual violence.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Consent must be freely given; silence from someone unable to consent is not consent.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents 6 hours after a sexual assault. She answers questions calmly, with flat affect and little visible emotion. A resident remarks that she "doesn't seem upset enough" and questions her account. Which statement best guides the team's interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calm affect shows she needs no mental health screen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Calm affect suggests the event was not traumatic

choices.label: C
choices.text: Emotional numbness is seen only after chronic abuse

choices.label: D
choices.text: Her lack of visible distress makes her account less credible

choices.label: E
choices.text: Responses vary, and no emotional state is diagnostic

explanation.summary: Responses to trauma vary widely; no specific mental state is diagnostic of or expected after an assault.
explanation.whyCorrect: People respond to traumatic experiences differently, and responses may include anxiety, anger, withdrawal, emotional numbness, hypervigilance, or no obvious emotional distress. No specific mental state is diagnostic of or expected after an assault, so her calm demeanor neither refutes her account nor removes the need for assessment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Assessment of emotional well-being and safety remains important regardless of affect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The event itself does not determine how a person experiences it, and calm affect does not mean it was not traumatic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Emotional numbness is listed among possible responses to trauma without restriction to chronic abuse.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No emotional state is expected after assault, so demeanor does not measure credibility.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman being treated for injuries from intimate partner violence agrees to a social work referral. Her employer calls the emergency department asking why she missed work. She asks that nothing about her visit be shared with him. Honoring this request most directly reflects which guiding principle of survivor care?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beneficence

choices.label: B
choices.text: Confidentiality

choices.label: C
choices.text: Justice

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nondiscrimination

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nonmaleficence

explanation.summary: Confidentiality means sharing only the necessary information as requested and agreed to by the survivor.
explanation.whyCorrect: The four guiding principles of a sensitive approach are safety, confidentiality, respect, and nondiscrimination. Confidentiality means sharing only the necessary information as requested and agreed to by the survivor, so withholding information from her employer at her request applies this principle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beneficence concerns acting for the patient's benefit, not restricting disclosure at her request.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Justice concerns fairness and allocation of resources, not information disclosure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nondiscrimination is providing appropriate care regardless of age, sex, ethnicity, religion, gender, or other factors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nonmaleficence concerns avoiding harm; confidentiality is the principle specifically at stake.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman requests an elective labiaplasty to alter otherwise normal genital anatomy after counseling. A colleague argues this should be handled exactly like female genital mutilation, and another suggests that reconstructive surgery after FGM should be treated the same way. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any change to normal genital anatomy is classified as FGM

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elective and reconstructive surgery are judged alike

choices.label: C
choices.text: FGM is acceptable where a community endorses it

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reconstruction after FGM is itself a form of FGM

choices.label: E
choices.text: These differ in indication and ethics; judge each apart

explanation.summary: FGM, medically indicated reconstruction, and elective procedures requested by informed adults differ in indications, decision-making, and ethics.
explanation.whyCorrect: FGM is distinct from medically indicated reconstructive procedures and from genital procedures requested by informed adult patients; these differ in clinical indications, decision-making processes, and ethical considerations. Elective procedures altering normal anatomy are evaluated separately from reconstructive procedures performed for medical reasons.

whyWrongByChoice.A: FGM is defined by non-medical removal or injury, and elective adult procedures are considered separately.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Elective procedures are evaluated separately from reconstructive procedures done for medical reasons.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FGM has no known health benefit and causes significant harm regardless of community endorsement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Medically indicated reconstruction is explicitly distinguished from FGM.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman presents for a routine visit accompanied by her partner, who answers most questions for her and insists on staying in the room. She makes little eye contact. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask the partner directly whether any violence occurs at home

choices.label: B
choices.text: Defer all screening until she comes in by herself

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have the partner confirm the details of her history

choices.label: D
choices.text: Offer her time alone, as is standard for every patient

choices.label: E
choices.text: Screen for abuse now with the partner in the room

explanation.summary: All patients should be given an opportunity to speak privately so sensitive topics and safety concerns can be assessed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clinicians should provide all patients with an opportunity to speak privately to facilitate discussion of sensitive topics and assessment of potential safety concerns, including coercion, controlling behaviors, and intimate partner violence. Framing private time as routine lets her speak without her partner present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Asking the possible perpetrator about violence compromises her safety and confidentiality.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Deferring may miss the only opportunity; private time should be offered now.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Relying on the partner for her history reinforces control and silences her.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Screening in front of a controlling partner may endanger her and prevent disclosure.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A physician is completing the chart for a 35-year-old woman who described being assaulted by a coworker. Which documentation practice is recommended?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Note the physician's opinion of how credible she seemed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Omit any statements not supported by exam findings

choices.label: C
choices.text: Record findings objectively, using her own words as relevant

choices.label: D
choices.text: Summarize her statements in the physician's interpretation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Translate her account into standard clinical terms for clarity

explanation.summary: Findings should be documented objectively, using the patient's own words when relevant.
explanation.whyCorrect: Recommended practices when obtaining a history of assault include documenting findings objectively using the patient's own words when relevant. Objective documentation also means patients need not repeatedly recount events that are adequately documented.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Credibility judgments are subjective and not part of objective documentation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Her statements should be recorded regardless of whether exam findings are present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Interpretive summaries replace her words with the physician's, which is not objective documentation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Converting her account into clinical terms loses her own words.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man returns to clinic 3 days after being sexually assaulted. His injuries are healing, but he reports that he cannot sleep and feels hopeless. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask directly about thoughts of self-harm or suicide

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid mental health questions to prevent distress

choices.label: C
choices.text: Diagnose PTSD today and start long-term psychotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassure him the feelings will fade on their own

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wait for him to raise emotional concerns himself

explanation.summary: After assault, clinicians should assess for thoughts of self-harm, suicide, or harm to others and refer for mental health support as appropriate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Assessment of emotional well-being and safety is an important component of care after assault. Clinicians should assess for thoughts of self-harm, suicide, or harm to others and refer for mental health evaluation or support when appropriate; hopelessness makes this assessment a priority.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Mental health and safety assessment is an important component of trauma care.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No specific mental state is diagnostic after assault; assessment and referral come first.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reassurance without assessment could miss suicidal thinking, a recognized consequence of trauma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clinicians should actively assess safety rather than wait for disclosure.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman with a long history of intimate partner violence has missed several appointments, drinks alcohol heavily, and has chronic back pain. She left the relationship 2 years ago. Which statement best explains her presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Missed visits indicate she was not seriously harmed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Substance use excludes a trauma-related explanation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trauma can impair care engagement and raise substance use

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trauma effects are limited to diagnosable psychiatric disorders

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trauma effects resolve once the violence has ended

explanation.summary: Trauma is a lasting response whose consequences include substance use, chronic pain, and difficulty engaging with health care.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trauma is a lasting physical, emotional, psychological, or behavioral response that can affect safety, trust, relationships, health, and engagement with medical care. Consequences include substance use, chronic pain and other physical conditions, and difficulty engaging with health care.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Difficulty engaging with health care is itself a consequence of trauma, not evidence against harm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Substance use is a recognized consequence of trauma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Consequences extend to physical, sexual, reproductive, and social health, not only mental health.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trauma is defined as a lasting response that can persist after the events end.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A physician is about to examine a 26-year-old woman who reports being assaulted the previous night. She has bruises on her arms and reports genital pain. How should the physical examination be sequenced?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Do a complete exam, leaving painful areas until last

choices.label: B
choices.text: Examine only the areas that she reports are injured

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have her fully undress at the start for efficiency

choices.label: D
choices.text: Omit the genital exam if the arms are the only injury

choices.label: E
choices.text: Start with the genital exam while findings are freshest

explanation.summary: Be complete and systematic, leaving private, painful, or stress-provoking portions of the examination for last.
explanation.whyCorrect: The clinician should be complete in the systematic examination and leave the private, painful, or stress-provoking portions for last, while allowing the patient to maintain clothing and modesty as much as possible, obtaining consent before sensitive portions, and screening for foreign bodies.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The examination should be complete and systematic, not limited to reported areas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Patients should maintain clothing and modesty as much as possible.
whyWrongByChoice.D: With genital pain reported, omitting that portion would be incomplete; it is done last with consent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sensitive, painful portions are left for last, not performed first.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl in Arkansas tells her physician she has had intercourse with a 20-year-old man. She insists that she wanted to and that she consented. Which statement about the Arkansas rape statute is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Her consent makes the activity lawful at her age

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her stated consent is not an absolute legal defense

choices.label: C
choices.text: The age-gap defense applies because she consented

choices.label: D
choices.text: The statute applies only to children younger than 12

choices.label: E
choices.text: The statute applies only when force can be shown

explanation.summary: Arkansas's rape statute covers sexual activity with a person younger than 14, and the younger person's consent is not an absolute defense.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arkansas's rape statute includes sexual intercourse or deviate sexual activity with a person younger than 14. There is a limited affirmative defense only when the actor is no more than three years apart in age, and consent by the younger person is not an absolute defense. A 7-year gap with a 13-year-old falls outside the limited defense.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Patient-reported consent does not equal legal consent; her age places this under the rape statute.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The limited defense depends on an age difference of no more than three years, which is not met here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The threshold in the statute is younger than 14, not 12.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This provision is based on age, not on proof of force.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: An 8-year-old girl is brought to a community emergency department for suspected sexual abuse. The on-call emergency medicine resident has no training in pediatric sexual abuse evaluation. Which of the following is most appropriate regarding the genital examination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A clinician credentialed in child maltreatment exams examines her

choices.label: B
choices.text: All medical care waits until law enforcement arrives

choices.label: C
choices.text: The resident examines her now to collect evidence quickly

choices.label: D
choices.text: The resident examines her with a parent as chaperone

choices.label: E
choices.text: The resident follows the adult sexual assault protocol

explanation.summary: Only clinicians with appropriate training should examine children for sexual abuse.
explanation.whyCorrect: Only clinicians with appropriate training should examine children (typically younger than 16), including understanding laws on consent, mandatory reporting, definitions of sexual violence against children, and who can collect and provide medico-legal evidence. Pediatric preparation is commonly separate from adult/adolescent training.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Medical care is not contingent on law enforcement processes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Speed does not justify an examination by someone without appropriate pediatric training.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A chaperone does not substitute for the examiner's required training.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Separate preparation is commonly required for pediatric versus adult/adolescent examinations.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy in Arkansas tells his physician he has recently become sexually active and asks about STI testing. The physician wants to determine whether child-protection or mandatory-reporting requirements might be implicated. Which information is most relevant to that determination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: His recent grades and school attendance

choices.label: B
choices.text: His total number of lifetime partners

choices.label: C
choices.text: The partner's age and any position of authority

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether he uses condoms consistently

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whether his parents approve of the relationship

explanation.summary: Whether reporting is implicated depends on age, age difference, voluntariness, coercion, capacity, power differential, exploitation, and safety.
explanation.whyCorrect: Different legal standards apply depending on the ages involved, the age difference, the nature of the conduct, and whether one person occupies a position of trust or authority. The clinician should assess age, age difference, voluntariness, coercion, capacity, relationship/power differential, exploitation, and immediate safety before deciding whether reporting is implicated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: School performance is not among the factors that determine reporting obligations.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Number of partners does not by itself indicate abuse or exploitation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Condom use matters for STI counseling but not for determining reporting requirements.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Parental approval does not change whether coercion, exploitation, or an age or power disparity exists.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: An emergency department calls in a Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) to see a 30-year-old woman who was assaulted 5 hours earlier. Which of the following best describes this professional's role?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arrest and formal interrogation of the suspected assailant

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forensic assessment, injury care, and evidence collection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Legal ruling on whether consent was actually given

choices.label: D
choices.text: Placement of the patient into emergency shelter housing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Psychiatric diagnosis and long-term psychotherapy

explanation.summary: A SANE is a specially trained clinician (e.g., RN) who performs forensic intake, treats injuries, and collects and preserves evidence.
explanation.whyCorrect: A SANE is a health care professional, such as a registered nurse, who has completed specialized education and supervised clinical training in caring for people who have experienced sexual assault. SANEs conduct forensic intake and assessment, assess and treat injuries, and collect and preserve evidence with specialized kits; many also provide expert testimony.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Apprehending suspects is a law enforcement function, not a clinical one.
whyWrongByChoice.C: SANEs may testify as experts, but legal determinations are made by the legal system.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Shelter placement falls to social work and advocacy services.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mental health professionals provide diagnosis and ongoing therapy.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman presents 3 days after a sexual assault and asks whether evidence can still be collected. A staff member tells her it is useless after 24 hours. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any clinician may collect evidence without special training

choices.label: B
choices.text: Collection should wait until all of her injuries have healed

choices.label: C
choices.text: Evidence collection is only useful in the first 24 hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: Evidence must be collected within 12 hours of the assault

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is often useful for several days; timeframes vary locally

explanation.summary: Forensic evidence is collected by trained professionals as soon as possible; it is often most useful within the first several days, and timeframes vary by jurisdiction.
explanation.whyCorrect: When indicated and desired by the patient, forensic evidence collection should be performed by a trained professional as soon as possible after the assault. Evidence collection is often most useful within the first several days, although applicable timeframes vary by jurisdiction and healthcare setting.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Evidence collection should be performed by a trained healthcare professional.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Evidence collection should occur as soon as possible, not be delayed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Evidence collection is often useful within the first several days, not only 24 hours.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No 12-hour cutoff is taught; timeframes vary by jurisdiction.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman treated for injuries from intimate partner violence says her top priorities are keeping her job and staying near her children's school. The resident proposes that she move immediately to a shelter in another city. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Build the safety plan around her own stated goals

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contact her employer to arrange a leave of absence

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have the social worker decide the plan without her input

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insist on the distant shelter since it is the safest option

choices.label: E
choices.text: Postpone any safety planning until she agrees to leave

explanation.summary: The patient's own goals and priorities should guide safety planning whenever possible.
explanation.whyCorrect: After acute needs are addressed, clinicians consider physical safety, housing, advocacy, pregnancy and STI prevention, mental health, follow-up, and social and financial resources, and the patient's own goals and priorities should guide safety planning whenever possible. Effective psychosocial support is patient-centered and responsive to individual needs.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Contacting her employer without her agreement breaches confidentiality.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Excluding her from the plan undermines autonomy and patient-centered support.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Imposing the clinician's preferred plan disregards her priorities and autonomy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Withholding safety planning until she complies abandons her in the meantime.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman's lacerations are repaired in the emergency department 10 hours after a sexual assault. Her vital signs are stable and she feels safe going to her sister's home. Which additional consideration is most important before she leaves?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cosmetic scar revision consultation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genetic carrier screening panel

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pregnancy prevention and STI evaluation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Routine fasting cholesterol screening panel

choices.label: E
choices.text: Routine vision and hearing screening

explanation.summary: After acute care, survivors need pregnancy prevention, STI evaluation/prevention/treatment, safety, advocacy, mental health, follow-up, and resources.
explanation.whyCorrect: After acute medical needs have been addressed, clinicians should consider immediate physical safety, housing or shelter needs, access to advocacy services, pregnancy prevention, STI evaluation, prevention, and treatment, mental health support, follow-up care, and social and financial resources. Sexual assault also carries risks of STIs and unintended pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cosmetic follow-up is not among the key post-assault domains.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Genetic carrier screening is unrelated to acute post-assault care.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Routine lipid screening is not a post-assault priority.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Routine sensory screening is not a post-assault priority.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman arrives in the emergency department with a bleeding forearm laceration after an assault. She asks that nothing be written in her chart because she fears legal consequences. Hospital policy requires documentation, and the team is unsure of its legal reporting obligations. Which of the following should the physician do first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Address her urgent medical needs, such as wound care

choices.label: B
choices.text: Agree to leave her visit entirely undocumented

choices.label: C
choices.text: Discharge her because she refuses documentation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hold treatment until hospital counsel clarifies the law

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfer her to a hospital with a different policy

explanation.summary: When legal or institutional requirements seem to conflict with patient needs, first identify immediate clinical needs and avoid abandonment or delay.
explanation.whyCorrect: When legal or institutional requirements appear to conflict with patient needs, clinicians should identify the immediate clinical needs, clarify the patient's goals and preferences, determine applicable legal and institutional requirements, seek ethics, legal, or administrative consultation when needed, and avoid abandonment or unnecessary delay in clinically appropriate care.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Legal and institutional requirements must be determined, not simply set aside.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Discharging her untreated is abandonment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Consultation may be sought, but delaying clinically appropriate care is to be avoided.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transferring to avoid policy is inappropriate and delays needed care.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman tells her physician that her family has arranged for her to marry a much older man next month and that she does not want to. A colleague says, "It's part of their tradition; we should stay neutral." Which response best reflects cultural humility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assume that her family's wishes reflect her own true values

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid the topic entirely so as not to cause offense

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recognize forced marriage as harmful while respecting her

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stay neutral, since the practice is culturally embedded

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tell her that her entire community's customs are harmful

explanation.summary: Cultural humility does not require treating every embedded practice as neutral; clinicians can respect the patient while recognizing coercive, harmful practices.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cultural humility does not require regarding every culturally embedded practice as medically or ethically neutral. A clinician can simultaneously seek to understand a practice, respect the patient's dignity, avoid stigmatizing a community, and recognize practices that cause harm, involve coercion, or violate autonomy; forced marriage is listed among such practices.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Patients are experts on their own values, which cannot be predicted from their community.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Avoidance fails to address a coercive practice she has raised.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neutrality ignores coercion that violates her autonomy; humility does not demand it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clinicians should avoid characterizing entire cultures or communities as harmful.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 20 weeks' gestation has a history of Type III female genital mutilation with a markedly narrowed vaginal opening. She is concerned about vaginal delivery. Which procedure surgically opens the infibulated vaginal opening?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clitoral reconstruction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deinfibulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Episiotomy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Labiaplasty

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reinfibulation

explanation.summary: Deinfibulation surgically opens the infibulated vaginal opening of Type III FGM and may facilitate intercourse, gynecologic care, or childbirth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Deinfibulation is a procedure that surgically opens an infibulated vaginal opening associated with Type III FGM. It may be performed to facilitate sexual intercourse, gynecologic care, or childbirth. Some individuals undergo reinfibulation after childbirth, leading to repeated procedures over a lifetime.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clitoral reconstruction does not open an infibulated vaginal opening.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Episiotomy is not the procedure described for opening an infibulated vaginal opening.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Labiaplasty is an elective procedure altering labial anatomy, not an opening of infibulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reinfibulation re-closes the opening after childbirth; it does the opposite.

questions.topicName: Gender-Based Violence, Trauma Informed Care, & Ethical Principles of Medical Care

questions.stem: A county health department opens a clinic offering counseling on contraceptive methods, prenatal monitoring through delivery, evaluation and treatment of infertility, and safe abortion services. Within the commonly accepted elements of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), these services most directly fall under which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reproductive health

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reproductive justice

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reproductive rights

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sexual health

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual rights

explanation.summary: Reproductive health covers contraception information, pregnancy and childbirth care, infertility treatment, and safe abortion services.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reproductive health is defined as access to information on the reproductive system and contraception, health care related to pregnancy monitoring and childbirth, infertility treatment services, and safe abortion services. Every service offered by this clinic falls within that element.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Reproductive justice is a framework about the social and structural conditions that make choice achievable; it is not one of the four SRHR elements.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reproductive rights are the rights to privacy, informed consent, and reproductive decisions free of stigma or discrimination, not the services themselves.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sexual health covers STI prevention and treatment, reproductive system cancers, and counseling for sexual dysfunction, not prenatal, infertility, or abortion care.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual rights concern access to information about sexuality and the pursuit of a safe and pleasurable sexual life; they are entitlements, not a service list.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man attends a clinic that offers treatment for gonorrhea and syphilis, screening for reproductive system cancers, and counseling for erectile dysfunction. These services best represent which element of sexual and reproductive health and rights?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bodily autonomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reproductive health

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reproductive rights

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sexual health

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual rights

explanation.summary: Sexual health covers STI prevention and treatment, reproductive system cancers, and counseling for sexual dysfunction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines sexual health as health care services for prevention and treatment of sexually transmitted infections and reproductive system cancers, plus counseling for sexual dysfunction and related disorders. STI treatment, cancer screening, and erectile dysfunction counseling match that definition exactly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bodily autonomy (bodily integrity and privacy) is a principle underlying SRHR, not the element that describes these clinical services.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reproductive health centers on contraception, pregnancy and childbirth, infertility, and safe abortion services, not STI treatment or sexual dysfunction counseling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reproductive rights are the rights to privacy, informed consent, and nondiscriminatory reproductive decisions, not a set of clinical services.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual rights concern access to information on sexuality and a safe, pleasurable sexual life, not STI or cancer services.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: An obstetrician in a state with a restrictive abortion law cares for a 29-year-old woman at 18 weeks' gestation with ruptured membranes and early signs of infection. The obstetrician is confident that ending the pregnancy is the medically and ethically appropriate course, but hospital attorneys instruct her to wait until the patient's condition clearly meets the statute's exception. She feels unable to do what she believes is right. Which concept best describes her experience?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conscientious objection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ethical uncertainty

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moral distress

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reproductive justice

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reproductive stigma

explanation.summary: Moral distress arises when a clinician knows the ethically appropriate action but external constraints, such as legal restrictions, prevent acting on it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Moral distress occurs when a health professional believes they know the ethically appropriate course of action but feels unable to act because of external constraints, including legal restrictions and institutional policy. The obstetrician is clear about what should happen; the law and hospital counsel prevent it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conscientious objection is declining to participate in care because it conflicts with one's own moral beliefs; here the physician wants to provide the care.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ethical uncertainty means being genuinely unsure which obligation should prevail; this physician is confident about the right course.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reproductive justice is a framework for how social and structural conditions shape reproductive choice, not a clinician's internal ethical experience.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stigma influences patients' care-seeking and access; it does not describe a clinician blocked from acting on a clear ethical judgment.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A family physician holds a deeply held religious belief against prescribing emergency contraception. A 22-year-old woman requests it 30 hours after unprotected intercourse, and the physician intends to decline. Which of the following actions best meets the professional responsibilities that remain for a conscientious objector?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arrange timely access to another clinician who will prescribe it

choices.label: B
choices.text: Counsel her that waiting for her next menses is equally effective

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decline and document the religious reason for refusal in her chart

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decline and let the patient locate another clinic on her own

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prescribe it anyway, since objection is not permitted in primary care

explanation.summary: Conscientious objection does not eliminate professional duties, including patient safety and timely access to care.
explanation.whyCorrect: A conscientious objection occurs when a clinician declines a specific aspect of care that conflicts with deeply held beliefs, but it does not eliminate professional responsibilities. The objector must still consider patient safety, timely access to care, nondiscrimination, and informed consent; ensuring prompt access to a willing prescriber satisfies these duties for a time-sensitive medication.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Giving inaccurate information violates informed consent and the duty to provide accurate information.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Documentation alone does nothing to secure the patient's safety or timely access to care.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leaving the patient to find care alone ignores the duty to preserve timely access for a time-sensitive treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conscientious objection is recognized; the issue is that it carries remaining responsibilities, not that it is forbidden.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: In 2022 the U.S. Supreme Court decided Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization. Which of the following best describes its holding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Established a federal statutory right to abortion nationwide

choices.label: B
choices.text: Extended constitutional contraception protection to unmarried individuals

choices.label: C
choices.text: Found no constitutional right to abortion, overturning Roe and Casey

choices.label: D
choices.text: Required every state to permit abortion before fetal viability

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upheld state limits on gender-affirming treatment for minors

explanation.summary: Dobbs (2022) overturned Roe v. Wade and Planned Parenthood v. Casey, holding that the Constitution does not confer a right to abortion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dobbs held that the U.S. Constitution does not itself confer a right to abortion, overturning Roe v. Wade (1973) and Planned Parenthood v. Casey (1992) and returning substantial authority to regulate abortion to elected governments. As a result, availability of some reproductive services now differs substantially by state.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dobbs was a constitutional ruling and created no federal statutory right to abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Extending contraception protection to unmarried individuals was Eisenstadt v. Baird (1972).
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dobbs did the opposite, removing a federal constitutional floor and leaving regulation to the states.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Upholding state restrictions on gender-affirming care for minors was United States v. Skrmetti (2025).

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman who is undocumented lives in a rural county without public transportation. She wants a contraceptive implant, but the nearest clinic is 90 miles away, she cannot afford the visit, and she fears that seeking care could expose her immigration status. Which framework best explains the gap between her legal right to contraception and her ability to use it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bodily autonomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conscientious obligation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ethical uncertainty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gender norms

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reproductive justice

explanation.summary: Reproductive justice recognizes that social, economic, political, and structural conditions determine whether people can meaningfully exercise reproductive choice.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reproductive justice holds that reproductive health is shaped not only by individual choice but by the conditions that determine whether that choice can be exercised. The lecture lists income, immigration status, geography, and access to health care among the factors that affect access, all of which block this patient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bodily autonomy is her right to decide, which she already holds; it does not explain why structural conditions prevent her from acting.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Conscientious obligation describes a clinician's felt duty to provide or advocate for care, not a patient's structural barriers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ethical uncertainty is a clinician's doubt about which obligation should prevail, not a barrier to patient access.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gender norms are socially constructed role expectations; nothing in the vignette involves them.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A maternal-fetal medicine physician counsels a 34-year-old woman at 20 weeks' gestation about a serious pregnancy complication. State law and hospital policy both permit either management option, and no colleague or administrator is pressuring the physician. After careful reflection, the physician remains genuinely unsure whether her duty to follow the patient's stated wishes or her duty to prevent a harm she foresees should take precedence. Which concept best describes the physician's situation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conscientious objection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conscientious obligation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ethical uncertainty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Institutional constraint

choices.label: E
choices.text: Moral distress

explanation.summary: Ethical uncertainty is genuine doubt about which ethical obligation should prevail, without external constraints blocking action.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ethical uncertainty asks, 'What is the right thing to do?' The clinician is genuinely uncertain which obligation should prevail. Because law and policy permit either course and nothing external is blocking her, this is not moral distress; she simply does not know which duty wins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conscientious objection is declining to participate because care violates one's moral commitments; she is not refusing any care.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Conscientious obligation is a clear sense that conscience requires acting to provide or advocate for care; she lacks that clarity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Institutional constraints are external limits such as hospital policy; the stem states policy permits either option.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Moral distress requires a clinician who knows the right action but is prevented from taking it by external constraints; she neither knows the answer nor faces a barrier.

choices.label: D

choices.label: E

explanation.summary: Adolescent pregnancy carries increased risk of eclampsia, postpartum endometritis, and systemic infections compared with pregnancy in the early twenties.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adolescent pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of certain maternal complications compared with pregnancy in the early twenties, specifically eclampsia, postpartum endometritis, and systemic infections. Postpartum endometritis is the listed complication among the choices.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fetal aneuploidy is not listed as an increased risk for adolescent patients.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gestational diabetes is not among the complications the lecture lists as increased in adolescent pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Placenta previa is not described as more common in adolescent pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Post-term pregnancy is not identified as a risk of adolescent pregnancy.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A family physician learns that many patients in her county cannot obtain contraceptive counseling. Believing that her ethical commitments and professional duties require her to provide and advocate for this care, she opens an evening clinic and lobbies her hospital to expand services. Her motivation is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conscientious objection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conscientious obligation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ethical uncertainty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moral distress

choices.label: E
choices.text: Paternalism

explanation.summary: Conscientious obligation is the belief that conscience requires a clinician to provide, facilitate, or advocate for care.
explanation.whyCorrect: A conscientious obligation describes a clinician's belief that she has a moral responsibility to provide, facilitate, or advocate for care because it is consistent with her ethical commitments and professional duties. It shows that conscience can motivate action, not only refusal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conscientious objection is declining to participate in care, the opposite of what she is doing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ethical uncertainty involves genuine doubt about the right course; she is clear about her duty.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Moral distress involves being blocked by external constraints; she is successfully acting on her beliefs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paternalism overrides patients' choices; she is expanding access to care patients are seeking.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy in Tennessee and his parents ask about gender-affirming hormone therapy, which state law restricts for minors. The parents ask what United States v. Skrmetti (2025) decided. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It banned gender-affirming care for minors in every state

choices.label: B
choices.text: It created a federal right to gender-affirming care for adults

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.text: It struck down the Tennessee law under the Equal Protection Clause

choices.label: E
choices.text: It upheld a state law, affirming broad state authority over minors' care

explanation.summary: Skrmetti upheld Tennessee's restrictions on certain gender-affirming treatments for minors without banning such care nationwide.
explanation.whyCorrect: United States v. Skrmetti upheld Tennessee's restrictions on certain gender-affirming medical treatments for minors, finding no Equal Protection violation under the arguments presented. It did not ban the care nationwide but affirmed that states have broad authority to regulate such care for minors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The decision explicitly did not ban gender-affirming care nationwide; it addressed one state's law.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No federal law grants a right to gender-affirming care, and Skrmetti concerned minors, not adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The case upheld restrictions on certain treatments; it did not leave all treatments legal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The Court found the law did not violate the Equal Protection Clause and upheld it.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old transgender woman presents for STI screening. Without asking, the clinician records her as attracted to men, reasoning that this follows from her gender identity. Which principle did the clinician overlook?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gender identity disclosure is rarely relevant to clinical care

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender identity is determined by the sex assigned at birth

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

whyWrongByChoice.C: Inferring orientation from any proxy repeats the clinician's mistake; the patient should be asked.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: The constitutional basis for providing contraception to an unmarried 19-year-old patient traces to a Supreme Court decision that extended protections previously recognized only for married couples. Which decision is this?

choices.label: A

explanation.summary: Eisenstadt v. Baird (1972) extended constitutional protection for contraception access to unmarried individuals.
explanation.whyCorrect: Griswold v. Connecticut (1965) protected married couples' use of contraception under marital privacy. Eisenstadt v. Baird (1972) extended that protection to unmarried individuals, broadening privacy protections beyond marriage.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Griswold (1965) protected contraception use by married couples only; it is the precedent Eisenstadt extended.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Obergefell (2015) recognized the right of same-sex couples to marry, not contraception access.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Casey (1992) concerned abortion and was overturned by Dobbs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Roe v. Wade (1973) concerned abortion and was overturned by Dobbs.

whyWrongByChoice.C: A primary health care conference is not the origin the lecture gives for SRHR.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman requests tubal ligation. Her husband calls the clinic, demands to know what she discussed, and insists she needs his approval. The clinician protects her confidentiality and proceeds on the basis of her own informed consent. Which SRHR element most directly underlies the clinician's actions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reproductive health

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reproductive justice

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reproductive rights

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sexual health

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual rights

explanation.summary: Reproductive rights are the right to privacy and informed consent and to make reproductive decisions without stigma or discrimination.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reproductive rights are defined as the right to privacy and informed consent and to make informed decisions on reproduction without stigma or discrimination. Protecting her confidentiality and relying on her own consent rather than her husband's approval honors these rights.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Reproductive health describes the services (the sterilization itself), not the privacy and consent protections at issue.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reproductive justice addresses structural conditions shaping choice, not the specific right to privacy and consent being protected here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sexual health refers to STI, reproductive cancer, and sexual dysfunction services, not the patient's privacy and consent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual rights concern information about sexuality and a safe, pleasurable sexual life, not reproductive decision-making.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A community organization campaigns for adults' entitlement to accurate information about sexuality and to pursue a safe and pleasurable sexual life. This campaign most directly advances which SRHR element?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bodily integrity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reproductive health

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reproductive rights

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sexual health

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual rights

explanation.summary: Sexual rights are the right to access information related to sexuality and to pursue a safe and pleasurable sexual life.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines sexual rights as the right to access information related to sexuality and to pursue a safe and pleasurable sexual life. The campaign's goals match this definition word for word in substance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bodily integrity is a principle fundamental to SRHR broadly, not the specific element defined by sexuality information and a safe sexual life.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reproductive health covers contraception, pregnancy, infertility, and abortion services.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reproductive rights concern privacy, informed consent, and reproductive decisions, not sexuality information or sexual life.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sexual health refers to clinical services for STIs, reproductive cancers, and sexual dysfunction, not an entitlement to information and a pleasurable sexual life.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: Which of the following best reflects the definition of sexual and reproductive health used in the SRHR framework?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of sexually transmitted infection, reproductive disease, and cancer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Access to contraception and prenatal care for all married adults nationwide

choices.label: C
choices.text: Freedom from dysfunction or infirmity affecting the reproductive organs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normal fertility and uncomplicated pregnancy outcomes across a population

choices.label: E
choices.text: Physical, emotional, mental, and social well-being in sexuality and reproduction

explanation.summary: Sexual and reproductive health is a state of physical, emotional, mental, and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sexual and reproductive health is defined as a state of physical, emotional, mental, and social well-being in relation to all aspects of sexuality and reproduction, not merely the absence of disease, dysfunction, or infirmity. The definition is deliberately broader than disease-free status.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The definition explicitly says SRH is not merely the absence of disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Access to services matters, but the definition is about well-being, and it is not restricted to married adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The definition states SRH is not merely the absence of dysfunction or infirmity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The definition concerns individual well-being across all aspects of sexuality and reproduction, not population fertility outcomes.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: Over the decades following the 1994 conference that introduced SRHR, a shift in perspective identified which pair of principles as fundamental to sexual and reproductive health and rights?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bodily integrity and personal privacy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Marital consent and family planning

choices.label: C
choices.text: Population control and fertility reduction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Religious freedom and conscience protection

choices.label: E
choices.text: State regulation and public health surveillance

explanation.summary: Bodily integrity and personal privacy are understood as fundamental to SRHR.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture describes a shift of perspective after which bodily integrity and personal privacy are understood to be fundamental to SRHR. Because all people are entitled to make decisions about their own bodies, sexual and reproductive health cannot be achieved without sexual and reproductive rights.

whyWrongByChoice.B: SRHR rights belong to individuals regardless of marital status; spousal consent is not a foundational principle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: SRHR centers on individual rights and well-being, not population-level fertility reduction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Conscience is discussed as a clinician consideration, not as a foundational principle of SRHR itself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: State regulation shapes access but is not described as a fundamental principle of SRHR.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: The United Nations incorporated elements of SRHR into its Sustainable Development Goals, including ensuring universal access to sexual and reproductive health care services such as family planning and integrating reproductive health into national strategies. explanation.whyCorrect: Elements of SRHR were incorporated into the UN Sustainable Development Goals for 2030, which call for universal access to sexual and reproductive health care services, including family planning, information and education, and integration of reproductive health into national strategies and programs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 2000 is not the target year given for the SRHR-related Sustainable Development Goals.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 2015 is not the target year; the goals are set for 2030.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 2020 is not the target year given in the lecture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 2025 is not the target year; the goals run to 2030.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

choices.text: Gender identity

choices.text: Legal restriction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moral distress

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stigma

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conscientious objection is a clinician declining to provide care; no clinician refused him.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nothing in the stem concerns his gender identity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No law prevented him from obtaining STI care; his barrier was fear of judgment.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A physician caring for a 32-year-old woman who recently immigrated assumes the patient will want her husband to make contraceptive decisions because of gender norms common in her country of origin. Which statement best identifies the error in this assumption?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gender norms apply only to behavior and not to health decisions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender norms are biologically fixed and cannot differ between spouses

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gender norms are learned solely within a person's family of origin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gender norms are uniform within a culture across generations

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gender norms vary and should not be assumed to describe any individual

explanation.summary: Gender norms are socially constructed, vary across and within cultures and over time, and should not be assumed to describe any individual.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gender norms are culturally and socially constructed expectations about behaviors and roles. They vary across societies, communities, and generations, can change over time, and should not be assumed to describe any individual person. The physician should ask the patient about her own preferences.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gender norms can affect healthcare choices, access, and participation in health decisions.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gender norms are socially and culturally constructed, not biologically fixed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Norms are learned through families, peers, schools, religious and cultural institutions, media, and other influences, not the family alone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Research documents variation in gender norms across communities, historical periods, and generations.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 26-year-old nonbinary patient reports delaying cervical cancer screening for years after a clinic's registration system required selecting either 'male' or 'female' and then would not schedule the test under the option the patient chose. choices.text: Administrative systems built on binary classification

choices.text: Confidentiality limits that apply to adolescents

choices.label: E
choices.text: Structural limits addressed by reproductive justice law

explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture notes that nonbinary and gender-nonconforming individuals may face challenges because administrative systems, clinical documentation, and treatment protocols rely on binary gender classifications. Some report delayed care or difficulty obtaining treatment as a result.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No clinician declined the screening on moral grounds; the registration system blocked it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The patient is an adult, and confidentiality was not the problem.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Moral distress is a clinician's experience, and no insurance restriction is described.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A physician weighs a patient's request for a procedure. She notes that the patient values it highly, that the clinical evidence supports it, and that state law permits it. choices.label: A
choices.text: A clinical evidence limit

choices.label: B
choices.text: A legal requirement

choices.label: C
choices.text: A personal value or belief

choices.label: D
choices.text: A professional responsibility

choices.label: E
choices.text: An institutional constraint

explanation.summary: Physicians must distinguish personal values, patient values, professional responsibilities, clinical evidence, institutional constraints, and legal requirements.
explanation.whyCorrect: Professional formation requires physicians to distinguish among personal values, the patient's values, professional responsibilities, clinical evidence, institutional constraints, and legal requirements. questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A married same-sex couple moves from one state to another and learns that their marriage must be recognized in every state because of a 2015 Supreme Court decision. That decision held which of the following?

choices.label: E

choices.text: Griswold v. Connecticut

choices.label: D

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: Reproductive justice encompasses three core rights: the right to have children, the right not to have children, and which of the following?

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clinician refusal relates to conscientious objection, not to the rights reproductive justice protects for individuals.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 13 weeks' gestation learns that prenatal testing shows a chromosomal abnormality in her fetus. She asks her physician what she should do. Consistent with contemporary professional guidance, which approach is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Defer all discussion until her partner can attend a visit

choices.label: B
choices.text: Explore her values and support the decision she reaches

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recommend continuing the pregnancy to avoid later regret

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recommend termination because of the expected medical burden

choices.label: E

whyWrongByChoice.D: Recommending termination directs her toward a particular outcome rather than respecting her values.

questions.topicName: Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights
